life_summary: Dieter Friedrich Uchtdorf was born on November 6, 1940, in Moravská Ostrava (now Ostrava), Czechoslovakia, in the Nazi-occupied Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia. His early life was marked by the hardships of World War II and the subsequent communist regime in Eastern Europe. He developed a passion for aviation and became a commercial airline pilot, eventually serving as a captain with Lufthansa. Before his full-time church service, Uchtdorf built a successful career in aviation spanning decades, combining his professional expertise with his deep religious convictions. He married Harriet Reich on December 14, 1962, in the Swiss Temple, and the couple established their family while balancing his demanding airline career with active church participation.
church_summary: Uchtdorf served as an Area President and later held positions in the Presidency of the Seventy before his 2008 appointment to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles. He has emphasized themes of family relationships, eternal perspectives, the spiritual significance of women, and the principle of lifting where one stands. He dedicated nine temples across multiple continents, including facilities in Honduras, Guatemala, Brazil, Florida, Argentina, Peru, Mexico, Colorado, and Arizona. His ministry has been characterized by a focus on gracious acceptance of divine callings and teaching members to neither seek nor decline assignments given to them by church leaders.
